evidence.intent_output: On the JDK the never-closed SSLSocketImpl holds no native resource and its finalizer close() returns at once once plain is closed (no finalizer-thread stall), so no JVM-side defect. The Android API 21 runtime (Conscrypt OpenSSLSocketImpl, fd-based) could not be exercised: Android device verification is out of scope for this run.

findings.title: Android: the never-closed Conscrypt SSLSocket keeps its native SSL state until GC and trips CloseGuard
findings.description: After the fix no SSLSocket is ever closed; only the plain socket under it. On the JDK this is harmless (verified). On Android (Conscrypt OpenSSLSocketImpl on API 21, ConscryptFileDescriptorSocket later) the SSL socket owns a native SSL*/SSL_CTX reference freed only by its finalizer, and its CloseGuard reports 'A resource was acquired ... but never released' for every https proxied request when StrictMode detectLeakedClosableObjects is on. Conscrypt's finalizer deliberately skips SSL_shutdown, so there is no stale-fd write; the cost is native memory held until GC plus StrictMode noise. Unproven on the target runtime.
findings.suggested_fix: Optionally, after the plain socket is closed (it is then closed, so the duplex close cannot wait), close the SSLSocket quietly as a second step on the same thread: ssl.close() returns immediately once the transport is closed (measured 0 ms on JDK 17), releasing native state on Android without reintroducing the TLS 1.3 wait. Keep the plain close first.

interaction_notes: RelayedBodyStream.close -> SocketBodyStream.close (plain only) -> exchange.release: read accounting (remaining, failure, abandoned) lives in read(), nothing depends on the inner stream's close; ChunkedBodyInputStream.close only forwarded to in.close().

http path: BackendClient.secure returns plain itself, so Attempt.plain and ProxyExchange.plain are the connection; connect() never returns null, so plain is never null on any path that builds an Attempt or a SocketBodyStream.

Retry: ProxyExchange.plain is overwritten by the next connect's plainSocket() before its connect, so a release after a failed retry connect/handshake closes the newest plain; the earlier plain was already closed before the wait.

TlsConnector watchdog and BackendClient.secure failure close only plain (unchanged); fire() closes plain (unchanged). After plain is closed a reader blocked in SSLSocketImpl fails at once; JDK 17 BaseSSLSocketImpl.finalize() -> close() also returns in 0 ms (measured), so no finalizer stall.
